content: Nafcillin for injection, USP, is a semisynthetic penicillin that is chemically derived from the penicillin nucleus, specifically 6-aminopenicillanic acid. The chemical name of nafcillin sodium is Monosodium (2S,5R,6R)-6-(2-ethoxy-1-naphthamido)-3,3-dimethyl-7-oxo-4-thia-1-azabicyclo[3.2.0]heptane-2-carboxylate monohydrate. This compound is resistant to degradation by the enzyme penicillinase, also known as beta-lactamase. Nafcillin sodium is provided as a sterile powder that ranges in color from white to yellowish-white and is intended for reconstitution prior to intravenous administration. Once reconstituted, the solution has a pH range of 6.0 to 8.5. Each Pharmacy Bulk Package of Nafcillin for injection, USP, contains nafcillin sodium in its monohydrate form, equivalent to 10 grams of nafcillin. The formulation is buffered with 40 mg of sodium citrate per gram of nafcillin, and the sodium content is approximately 65 to 78 mg per gram. The Pharmacy Bulk Package is a sterile container designed to hold multiple single doses. It is specifically intended for use in pharmacy admixture programs and is restricted to the preparation of intravenous infusion admixtures. It is important to note that further dilution of the reconstituted solution is required before administration. Detailed instructions for reconstitution, dilution, and proper use of the Pharmacy Bulk Package can be found in the sections on Dosage and Administration and Directions for Proper Use of Pharmacy Bulk Package.
